goal: Deleting a short link must remove its analytics so a re-created alias starts with zero clicks, and already-orphaned data must be repaired
functional: After DELETE /api/links/{code}, no click rows for that code remain
Re-creating the same alias yields stats with total_clicks 0 and empty by-day and referrer breakdowns
On startup, click rows whose link does not exist are removed (idempotent)
Public API (routes, request and response shapes, Python signatures) is unchanged
ambiguities: Should orphaned historical clicks be purged or archived? Assumed purge: they are unreachable through the API and have no owner
Is 'delete' a hard delete? Assumed yes, matching current behaviour of DELETE /api/links/{code}
Should the fix rely on SQLite foreign keys alone? Assumed no: delete explicitly as well, so correctness does not depend on a per-connection pragma
acceptance: Regression test fails on the current code and passes after the fix
All previously passing tests still pass and none are removed
Public API signatures are backward compatible
Changes are limited to the symbols declared in the impact analysis
